subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser-login handoff surface be a core Control UI page, a bundled browser-plugin tab using the plugin UI seam, or wait for the generic plugin UI entry-point design to land first?
rationale: The requested behavior is valid, but exposing authenticated browser state and resume controls crosses product UX, operator-scope, redaction, and plugin/core ownership boundaries that automation should not decide.

options.title: Design bundled browser handoff tab
options.body: Define an admin-scoped bundled browser plugin or native panel with status, tab list, focus/open/close actions, manual-action state, and same-profile resume semantics.

options.title: Wait for generic plugin UI entry points
options.body: Keep this blocked on the broader plugin UI entry-point API if maintainers want browser UI to be just another plugin-owned panel.

options.title: Fold into broad browser preview tracker
options.body: Merge the handoff scope into the broader remote preview effort, accepting a larger design and implementation surface.

recommendation.title: Design bundled browser handoff tab
recommendation.body: Define an admin-scoped bundled browser plugin or native panel with status, tab list, focus/open/close actions, manual-action state, and same-profile resume semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest product signal is the maintainer comment marking this issue as canonical, and recent Control UI navigation work also routes naturally there.
